frontier.hypothesis: The last 2 instructions are the two `addu a3,a0,zero` copies, and they are a whole-function pointer-live-range property — not a preheader spelling and not a C-level copy.
frontier.mechanism: In target the loop-1 pre-guard pointer a0 is live-out on the entry guard's TAKEN edge: the `blez` at 0x800178C8 jumps to .L8001791C, which consumes a0 as loop 2's guard operand on the skip path. Because a0 must survive that edge, the preheader cannot overwrite it with the loop base, so the allocator emits the copy and then `addu a0,a1,a3`. Every form built so far lets the guard pointer DIE at the branch, so the allocator overwrites it and no copy appears. Both C-level routes to a copy are now closed by name (cse.c, combine.c — H-s6-2/H-s6-3), so the only remaining route is to give the pointer a live range that spans the taken edge.
frontier.next_probe: Build a form where ONE pointer variable is read fresh after each join, used by that loop's entry guard, AND still read by the NEXT guard on the skip path. Concretely: a single `p` assigned before loop 1's guard and re-assigned only in loop 1's EXIT TAIL (after the do/while, not before loop 2's guard) — which is exactly the data flow the target asm shows. Start from variant D (rejected/base_from_pre_join_pseudo_defeats_cse_fold_costs_1.c), NOT from candidate B, because D already has the pre-guard read and the un-folded addus. Read tmp/grind/func_80017848/s6/G/ings_pp.c.greg for reg/v77's conflict and preference records before writing C, and re-dump with s6/probe.sh after each attempt.

frontier.hypothesis: Every s3/s4/s5 spelling conclusion was measured ON the divergent chassis and must be treated as chassis-relative until re-measured on the correct one.
frontier.mechanism: The divergence deleted two pointer reloads, which shifted register pressure and scheduling across the whole preheader region; rankings measured against a 125-insn build that was 2 short for a SEMANTIC reason do not transfer to a correct 125-insn build. s5 already learned a weaker form of this (its shift-first conclusion turned out chassis-relative to s4's `base = slots;`, and then turned out to be a dead-declaration artifact on top of that). What DOES survive untouched is the pass-level kills (H-s6-2, H-s6-3), because they are RTL facts rather than score comparisons.
frontier.next_probe: Before spending ANY banked spelling conclusion, re-run it as a matched pair against the current candidate with s6/score.sh (one blocking call per ~6 cells, cells generated with a per-cell-pruned declaration block per s5's process rule 1). Do NOT re-open a broad preheader sweep — the point is targeted re-validation of a conclusion about to be used, not another 50-cell grid.

frontier.hypothesis: The top-block 4-instruction shadow is still downstream of the preheader property and should still not be attacked directly.
frontier.mechanism: Unchanged from s5: target's second `bltz` has a `nop` delay slot because the first instruction of its target block is `lw a0,0xC(s2)`; ours has `sll a1,s4,6` there and reorg.c's fill_slots_from_thread steals it into the slot, retargeting the branch to label+4. Variant D already places a `lw` first in that block, so this may resolve for free once frontier item 1 moves.
frontier.next_probe: After ANY movement on frontier item 1, re-diff with s6/dis.sh and check whether the `bltz` delay slot became a `nop` without further work. Only if it did NOT should reorg.c's non-own-thread fill_slots_from_thread path be read as its own mechanism.
